cases.title: When CE works out the other end from the grade, the level you typed is drawn exactly (1.10 stays 1.10, never 1.11)
cases.plan_item: BUG-025 carpark retest (CARPARK_RETEST_TRIAGE_29OCT.md); BUG-026 is the same stored-level fault seen in the Inspector
cases.expected: A third reset pipe (150000,-104000 to 160000,-104000, Standard grade, work-out off, 18.000 and 17.900, label on) puts the remembered New Pipe values back; it is recorded, not judged. Pipe A (CD 150000,-96000 to 160000,-96000, custom grade 1 in 100, 'I know one end' on, upstream known, known level 1.10): its IL texts read 1.10 at the 150000 end and 1.00 at the 160000 end. Pipe B (CD 150000,-100000 to 151000,-100000, same grade, downstream known, known level 1.10): the IL text at the 151000 end reads 1.10 (the typed level, never 1.11) and the one at the 150000 end reads 1.12. No grade mismatch window opens. The drawing file on disk is unchanged.
cases.why_not_unit: The unit tests check the rounding helper on its own; only a live CD shows that the New Pipe window passes the typed level and the chosen end to it and that the drawn IL text carries the result.
not_automated: The CE Inspector's grade figure (BUG-026) is not read: the Inspector palette has never been read by a case. A Codex look is listed for it in the triage report.
The Edit Pipe route (CDEDIT with the work-out toggle) is not driven. The window's own preview of the worked-out level is recorded, not checked.
Tim's own value of inverts.minOutletDropMm is not read; 1.12 assumes the shipped 20 mm. If Pipe B's upstream reads another value, read the setting before calling it a fault.

cases.title: A pipe with only its first level typed (Standard grade) gets a label ending in the grade number, with no MIN.
cases.plan_item: BUG-027 carpark retest (CARPARK_RETEST_TRIAGE_29OCT.md); Tim's ruling UX-CPLAN-05 of 26 Sep 2026
cases.expected: CD from 150000,-96000 to 170000,-96000 with Standard grade, 'I know one end' off, the first level 18.000 and the second level switched off: Start Pipe gives exactly one pipe and one label matching '<size> DIA. <material> PIPE AT 1 IN <n>' with nothing after the number, never 'MIN.'. Exactly one IL text (IL 18.000). A reset pipe (150000,-100000 to 170000,-100000, both levels) follows and is recorded. The drawing file on disk is unchanged.
cases.why_not_unit: The unit test GradeAutoCalcTests asserts the opposite (100 MIN.); only the drawn label in a live CD shows what the drafter gets.
not_automated: Edit Pipe's twin path (PipeEditCommand.GradeText.cs line 290) is not driven.
How the label looks is not judged; only its words.

cases.title: On a pipe falling slightly to the south-east (92 and 96 degrees), both IL texts set to Above sit above the pipe line
cases.expected: Two 20 m pipes drawn with CD, levels 18.000 and 17.900, IL texts on Above (the default): pipe A 150000,-96000 to 170000,-96698 and pipe B 150000,-100000 to 170000,-102096. Each pipe gets exactly one IL 18.000 within 1000 mm of its first end and one IL 17.900 within 1000 mm of its second end, and every one of the four sits above the pipe line: A first y > -96035, A second y > -96698, B first y > -100105, B second y > -102096. The drawing file on disk is unchanged.
cases.why_not_unit: The unit tests check the perpendicular angle on its own; only a drawn pipe shows which side the live text writer puts the IL text on, after clash nudging.
not_automated: A truly vertical pipe (the west-is-top fallback) and Edit Pipe's round trip are not drawn. Whether the text reads well is a Codex look.

The drawing file on disk is unchanged.
cases.why_not_unit: The fault came from AutoCAD's live UCS during a CE command; only a real insert under a rotated UCS shows the block's stored rotation.

Align to pipe and Align to building orientations are not driven. Whether the pit label and cover text are square is not read.
